sections.h2: What kind of place is Walker County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Walker County fills Georgia's northwest corner, right against the Tennessee line, and its northern end belongs to the Chattanooga commuting zone. State lawmakers formed it on December 18, 1833, out of former Cherokee territory, and the seat is LaFayette, per Wikipedia.

At 447 square miles, it holds ridges, caves and coves rather than flat farmland: Lookout Mountain, Pigeon Mountain, McLemore Cove and a slice of the Chattahoochee National Forest. A listing can therefore be a lot in town, a mountainside tract or acreage in a valley. Five incorporated cities sit inside it (Chickamauga, LaFayette, Lookout Mountain, Rossville and a small piece of Fort Oglethorpe), and Rock Spring, Fairview, Lakeview and Chattanooga Valley are census-designated places.

The Walker County School District covers most of the county, while Chickamauga has its own city system. Four of five county commission seats are tied to districts called Rossville, Chickamauga, LaFayette and Lookout Mountain, which gives a rough picture of where residents live. The Chattooga and Chickamauga Railway still runs on part of the old rail corridor.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Walker County homes?
sections.html:
Walker County leans heavily toward homeowners, and prices run under the national figure. The numbers below come from the Census Bureau.

Residents numbered 67,654 on census day in 2020, slightly below the 68,756 of 2010, and the July 2025 estimate is 70,250. The 2020 count showed 28.2% of occupied homes rented, 10.1% of all units empty and a median age of 41.6. About 51% of residents lived in rural areas, which fits the mix of hillside and valley parcels.

sections.h2: Which offices handle Walker County property tax?
sections.html:
Billing sits with the Tax Commissioner and valuation sits with the Board of Tax Assessors. The commissioner's site says its office neither determines property value nor sets the tax rate.

  • Rock Spring: 122 Highway 95, mail to P O Box 510, Rock Spring, GA 30739, phone 706-638-2929, weekdays 8:00 A.M. until 4:30 P.M., with a drop box beside the front entrance.
  • Rossville: 2012 McFarland Gap Road in the Fairview community, same phone and hours.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: 706-638-4823, the number the commissioner lists for preferential assessment questions.
  • Search and pay online at walkercountytax.com.

Two offices give owners on the Tennessee side of the county and those near Rock Spring a nearer counter. Ask either location for the county and school levy lines so you can see how the bill is built.

sections.h2: When does Walker County property tax come due?
sections.html:
The county ties the deadline to the mailing date: payment is due 60 days after notices go out, which the commissioner says lands on December 20 in most years. Whatever date prints on your bill is the one that counts.

By mail, only a USPS postmark is honored, and a metered mark does not qualify. Georgia's Department of Revenue adds that interest does not begin until 60 days after the bill's postmark, and penalties may follow later on any unpaid balance.

  • Manufactured homes located in the county on January 1 are due April 1 each year and carry a 10% penalty plus 1% monthly interest when late, with a possible State Court citation.
  • The value date is January 1, so anyone who closes on a purchase after that date should confirm that the bill reaches them.

sections.h2: What is the appeal route for a Walker County value?
sections.html:
Written appeals must reach the assessors within 45 days after the notice date. The grounds are taxability, value or uniformity, and a complaint that the bill is too high does not count.

The board reviews first, a Board of Equalization hearing comes next, and Superior Court is the last stop; arbitration is available as a substitute for the hearing. An owner who disagrees with the carried-forward value can also file a new return between January 1 and April 1. Georgia sets assessed value at 40% of market value, so the number on your notice for tax purposes is smaller than the market figure.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and credits does Walker County list?
sections.html:
The commissioner's site lists state and local homestead exemptions, and the local amount wins whenever it is larger than the state one. Bring the warranty deed if this is your first application.

  • Standard homestead: printed as $2,000 for state, school and county purposes.
  • County senior exemptions start at age 70, with a $15,000 adjusted gross income cap on the county-tax version and a separate county school exemption, while a county school exemption for owners 75 and older carries the same cap.
  • Disabled veteran and armed forces surviving spouse exemptions: the page prints $81,080.
  • Tax deferral: ages 62 and up with gross household income of $15,000 or less, until a change of ownership or until deferred tax plus interest reaches 85% of market value.
  • 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant: the page says it lowers assessed value by $18,000 for credit purposes and shows on the 2026 bill if a homestead exemption was on file by April 1, 2026. Rentals and investment property do not receive it.

Applications arriving after April 1 take effect the following year, and an approved exemption renews itself until ownership or residence changes.

sections.h2: How does a Walker County sale handle unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Get a written balance from the Tax Commissioner, and let the closing agent send it to the county out of your proceeds. State practice allows unpaid property to be levied and sold, which is why a balance should not be left for the buyer to find.

Check any manufactured home on the land separately, since its tax follows the April 1 schedule instead of the autumn one. Inherited houses and rentals can have more than one tax year open, so request the status of each. With 28.2% of occupied homes rented in 2020 and a stock that stretches from hillside cabins to town lots, buyers who take houses as they stand are a natural audience, and a cash sale can pay the county first without a repair list.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Walker County real estate tax?
faqs.a: Sixty days after the bills are mailed, which the county says is December 20 in most years. The date on your own bill governs.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Walker County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: Dial 706-638-2929. The Rock Spring and Rossville counters are open weekdays from 8:00 A.M. to 4:30 P.M. The Board of Tax Assessors uses 706-638-4823.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a Walker County assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the mailing date on the notice. The Board of Tax Assessors hears it first, then the Board of Equalization if the dispute continues.

faqs.q: Where is a Walker County homestead exemption filed?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner's office, by April 1 of the first year you want the benefit. New owners should carry the warranty deed, and the exemption then renews without a new form.

faqs.q: Can a Walker County house be sold while taxes are owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent pays the county from your proceeds once the commissioner supplies a written balance. List every open year if the house was rented or inherited.
